narrative: Material PL3__M7544772 exhibits regular demand with a coefficient of variation of 0.62 and high demand stability (78.5% non-zero days). The current SAP policy (safety stock 225, order quantity 225) results in excessive ordering costs ($160,064/year) due to severe under-batching relative to actual daily consumption. The optimized (r,Q) policy increases safety stock to 3,487 units to meet the 95% service level target and sets a storage-capacity-constrained order quantity of 7,157 units, yielding annual cost savings of $150,485 (93.9% reduction). Lead time instability (CV=0.81) is the dominant driver of safety stock and warrants supplier SLA review.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Regular demand regime with 78.5% non-zero days and stable mean warrants a continuous-review (r,Q) model; EOQ minimises ordering vs holding cost trade-off with capacity cap applied.
research_insights.boundary_risk: EOQ of 10,325 units exceeds available storage headroom above safety stock; order quantity capped at 7,157 units, increasing order frequency from 46 to 67/year and slightly raising ordering costs.

warnings: High lead time variability (CV=0.81); consider supplier diversification or SLA enforcement
